text: Right where we left off. A goblin no taller than Jaeha's waist is holding a boss's sword off with one knife, and he isn't even out of breath.
He hadn't noticed the blood. Years of walking into traps first have taught him not to notice pain.
The goblin spins out from under the blade and kicks the giant sword aside with his bare heel.
Then he grabs Yerin by the collar and Jaeha by the vest and drags them both across the floor like luggage.
A heartbeat later, the sword smashes the spot where they were sitting.
Behind a pillar, a window opens in front of Jaeha. Summon answered: Nib. Far Side scout. Seal one of five. Field form: five minutes.
So the goblin has a name: Nib. He doesn't ask where he is, or how he got here. A soldier asks about the enemy first.
Jaeha answers the way he'd fill in a form, as if it were the most normal job in the world.
Nib doesn't even blink. A scout knows that job well.
Yerin hugs her bag tighter. Nothing in a healer's training covers a husk with opinions.
There's no time to explain. The knight drags its sword out of the floor and turns toward their pillar.
Jaeha has never given an order in his life, so he reaches for the only rule anyone ever gave him.
For a second, Nib almost smiles.
And he's gone, a dark streak across the hall.
From above, you can see how unfair this is: a goblin barely a metre tall, charging a knight four and a half metres high.
His knives rake the back of its knee, and the armour barely scratches.
A window explains why. Nib's seal limits him to twenty percent of his real power.
He's fighting at a fraction of his old strength, and he still runs straight up the knight's sword.
He slashes at the hole where its face should be, but the knight jerks back, and the knife skids off the helm.
Then a huge gauntlet comes round and swats him out of the air.
Nib flies across the hall and craters a pillar. Three minutes thirty-one seconds left.
Jaeha shouts his name before he can stop himself.
Nib lands on his feet in the rubble and spits, already reading the fight.
Jaeha writes down every trap he walks into. Tonight the trap is a knight, and his notes end in a question.
A thin amber thread runs from Jaeha's fingertips to Nib. The moment he reaches along it, the system names it: Link. Nib's eyes, silent orders, and Nib's pain.
Suddenly Jaeha is looking out of Nib's eyes, straight up at the knight.
That's the price of Link: every hit Nib takes, Jaeha feels too.
Through Nib's eyes, there it is: a crack in the knight's left shoulder plate.
So Jaeha does what he has never been allowed to do on a raid: he calls the play.
Nib's ear twitches. The link works both ways.
So Jaeha thinks instead, and counts, the way he counted the lizard's bites.
The plate dips.
Now! Nib drops flat, and the blade passes a finger's width over his back.
Then he springs up inside the knight's guard and rips both knives along the seam under its arm. Violet ash sprays out like blood.
The knight clutches its shoulder. Something finally hurt it. Two minutes fourteen.
Yerin stares at Jaeha. On a raid, nobody listens to the trap-tester.
But the knight whirls back faster than ever and drives its pommel down at Nib like a hammer. Crouched low, Nib has no room to dodge.
A second window offers a trade: Carry. Jaeha can take part of Nib's damage into his own body. Too much, and he bleeds, then collapses. It's asking, not giving.
Jaeha doesn't even read the warning twice.
The pommel slams down on Nib, and half of the blow simply vanishes into a ring of amber light.
Because across the hall, Jaeha takes it. He folds to his knees, fresh blood running from his nose. Fifty percent of the hit, moved to the Operator.
Half of the blow meant for Nib lands on Jaeha's body instead, and Yerin can't see where it came from.
But Nib understands. And for the first time, the deadpan goblin looks shocked.
He's back at the pillar in a blink. In all his years as a soldier, no officer ever took a blow for him.
Jaeha grins through the blood, as if the answer were obvious.
Nib doesn't answer. The look in his eye says nobody has ever done that for him before.
He turns away before anyone can see his face and points a knife at the healer.
Yerin's hands are shaking. A soft mint light gathers in them anyway. One minute twenty left.
Earlier tonight she froze in front of a lizard. Now she kneels in a boss room with both hands on his wound.
The nosebleed stops. The smile Jaeha gives her is a real one.
Jaeha gets back on his feet, notebook open, already hunting for the next opening.
But the knight has gone completely still. Forty seconds left on Nib's clock.
Then it throws back its head and roars, in a language nobody in Seoul has ever heard.
The roar shakes dust from the ceiling. Behind the pillar, nobody understands a word of it. Nobody but Nib.
Nib doesn't cover his ears. He just stares.
At the badge on the knight's chest: a wall with nine towers.
He knows that wall. He says its name like a prayer.
Jaeha has never heard of it. But he has never heard Nib's voice sound like that, either.
Nib lowers his knives and looks up at the giant that nearly killed them all.
